def: An element of a library function specification: the conditions for the function to participate in overload resolution. When not met, the function is silently non-viable, which can be observed by requires-expressions and type traits (SFINAE-friendly).

An element of a library function specification: conditions whose violation makes the program ill-formed (diagnosis required). Usually implemented with a static_assert in the function body, so it cannot be detected by a requires-expression.

An element of a library function specification: conditions the function assumes to hold on every call; violating any precondition is undefined behavior. An implementation may, but need not, check them with contract assertions.

A condition listed in the Hardened preconditions element of a library function specification. In a hardened implementation, the corresponding contract assertion is evaluated with a terminating semantic at the call; in a non-hardened implementation, a violation is undefined behavior.

The way library specifications describe a function's semantics with code: the function's own Constraints/Mandates apply first, all specification elements of the calls in the code are carried over, and the function's own Throws/Postconditions/Complexity override them. It specifies observable semantics and does not constrain how it is implemented.

A set of valid-expression requirements given in tables and named in italics with a Cpp17 prefix (such as Cpp17CopyConstructible). Unlike library concepts in monospace font, it is only a textual requirement, and failing to meet it is usually undefined behavior.

An entity introduced in the library specification to describe semantics, whose comment ends in exposition only (such as decay-copy, or expository private members). Programs cannot name them, and implementations need not provide them.
An exposition-only function: returns, by copy-initialization, a copy of its argument after decay (decay_t). Close to auto(x), but with a convertible_to constraint and using copy-initialization.

A library type that can be implemented as an enumeration with overloaded bitwise operators, an integer type, or a bitset (such as ios_base::fmtflags). Only its elements and operations such as &, |, ^, ~ can be relied upon; set/clear/is set have precise definitions.
A library type that can be implemented as an enumeration or a synonym for an enumeration (such as ios_base::seekdir), whose enumerated elements have distinct values.
A character sequence whose highest-addressed element with defined content has the value zero and all of whose other elements are non-zero. A string literal is a static ntbs.
An ntbs that constitutes a sequence of valid multibyte characters, beginning and ending in the initial shift state.

A customization point object specified as a set of overloaded function templates (such as std::ranges::find, colloquially a niebloid). Calling it is expression-equivalent to calling that set of function templates; it is not found by ADL, and suppresses ADL when found by unqualified lookup.
A declaration, entity, or macro that must be present in both freestanding and hosted implementations; determined by the freestanding comments in the synopses and their inheritance rules.

A function declaration whose comment in the synopsis contains freestanding-deleted. Whether it is a deleted function on a freestanding implementation is implementation-defined, to prevent overload resolution from silently changing when migrating to a hosted implementation.

Library facilities that a hosted implementation must provide and a freestanding implementation need not. A freestanding implementation may provide an implementation-defined subset of them, or provide deleted definitions for functions among them.
The C++ library headers in Table 24 (for a freestanding implementation, the subset it provides), which can be imported as header units; the C facility headers are not among them.

A call to a library function that prevents the enclosing expression from being a core constant expression. E.g. a call to a C library function that raises a floating-point exception other than FE_INEXACT.

t is swappable with u: in a context where both the swap templates in <utility> and the results of ADL are considered, swap(t, u) and swap(u, t) are both valid and actually exchange the values of the two.
An explicit specialization or partial specialization that is not part of the standard library and not defined by the implementation. Its instantiations are also program-defined types.

A standard library function explicitly designated as one whose address may be taken (such as the iostream manipulators std::endl, std::hex, and the functions in <meta>). Forming a pointer, reference, or pointer to member to any other standard library function has unspecified behavior (possibly ill-formed).
A name left behind by a facility removed from the standard (auto_ptr, bind1st, <codecvt>, …), still reserved for previous standardization; programs must not use it for other purposes.

Whether or not T is complete, the allocator class X and the member types of allocator_traits<X> other than value_type are complete types. This is the prerequisite for vector/list/forward_list being allowed to be instantiated with incomplete types.

Two allocator pointer values (possibly of different types) that compare equal after being converted to const_pointer by a sequence of static_casts only among pointer/const_pointer/void_pointer/const_void_pointer.
